members.bio: Backend developer. Likes tidy logs and long walks.
Tinkers with home servers and old laptops.
Data engineer by day, amateur baker by night.
Runs a small hosting company. Ask me about DNS.
Teacher learning to code, one project at a time.
Mobile developer. Coffee, cycling and too many side projects.
Writes documentation and reads too many changelogs.
Student. Building a game engine nobody asked for.

forums.name: General
forums.description: Introductions, everyday chat and anything that does not fit elsewhere
forums.guidance: Say hello, share what you are up to and keep it friendly.

threads.title: Welcome! A note about the sample content
threads.body:
Hello and welcome. Everything you see here right now (the members, forums, threads and replies) is sample content that was added when this forum was installed.

It is here so you can see how lists, threads, replies and nested replies look before real conversations start. Browse around, try the search and the reading settings, and edit or remove it when you are ready.

threads.title: Introduce yourself
threads.body:
New here? Tell us a little about yourself: what you do, what you are working on and what brought you to the forum.

I will start: I write backend services for a living and spend weekends hiking with a camera I barely know how to use.

threads.title: What are you working on this week?
threads.body:
A weekly thread for small updates. It does not have to be impressive: fixing a leaky tap counts.

This week I am finally moving my notes out of three different apps into plain text files.

threads.title: A productivity habit that actually stuck
threads.body:
Most productivity advice does not survive the first busy week. Which habit did survive for you?

Mine is boring: I write tomorrow's first task on a sticky note before I close the laptop.

threads.title: Books you read this year and would recommend
threads.body:
Fiction or non-fiction, technical or not. One line on why you liked it is plenty.

I will go first with a history of the shipping container. It is far more interesting than it sounds.

threads.title: Coffee, tea or something else?
threads.body:
Settling an office argument. What gets you through the morning, and how do you make it?

Bonus points for unreasonable equipment.

threads.title: Show us your desk setup
threads.body:
Post a photo or just describe it. Standing desk, kitchen table, a laptop on the sofa: all welcome.

I recently moved my monitor up to eye level and my neck has stopped complaining.

threads.title: Learning something new as an adult
threads.body:
I started piano lessons at 34. Progress is slow, but it is the only hour of the week when I am not thinking about work.

What have you picked up later in life, and how do you stay motivated?

threads.title: Small wins thread
threads.body:
Share something that went right recently, however small.

Mine: I fixed a bug on the first try today and had no idea what to do with the extra hour.

threads.title: How do you take breaks during the day?
threads.body:
I am bad at stepping away from the screen. Timers, walks, stretching apps, a dog that demands attention?

Looking for ideas that do not need much willpower.

threads.title: Recommend a podcast
threads.body:
Long commute coming up and my playlist is empty. Any topic, as long as the hosts do not shout.

I enjoy anything about how everyday things are designed or made.

threads.title: What was your first computer?
threads.body:
Mine was a beige tower with a turbo button that, as far as I could tell, did nothing.

What was yours, and what did you mostly use it for?

threads.title: Weekend plans?
threads.body:
Anything fun lined up? I am planning to do absolutely nothing, and I am looking forward to it.

Tell us about yours.

threads.title: Working from home: what changed for you?
threads.body:
A few years in, what do you miss about the office, and what would you never give up?

For me: no commute, but I talk to the cat far more than is healthy.

threads.title: Cooking for one without wasting food
threads.body:
Recipes are always for four. How do you shop and cook when it is just you?

I have started freezing portions, but I am running out of freezer.

threads.title: The best advice you ever got at work
threads.body:
Something a colleague or manager said that stuck with you.

Mine: "Write down the decision and the reason, not just the decision." It has saved me from the same argument more than once.

threads.title: Hobbies that have nothing to do with screens
threads.body:
Gardening, climbing, woodworking, knitting? What do you do to get away from the computer?

I have just started growing chillies on the balcony.

threads.title: Favourite game of the year so far
threads.body:
Board games, video games, puzzles: what kept you up too late recently?

We have been playing a cooperative card game every Friday and losing every single time.

threads.title: How did you find this forum?
threads.body:
Curious how people end up here: a search, a friend, a link in a changelog?

I followed a link from a blog post about self-hosting and never left.

threads.title: Late-night thoughts
threads.body:
A thread for half-formed ideas that do not deserve a topic of their own.

Tonight's: why do all the good ideas arrive right after you close the laptop?

replies: Welcome aboard! Glad you found us.
Same here, I thought I was the only one.
This made me smile, thanks for posting.
I tried that last year and it stuck for about two weeks. Maybe I will give it another go.
Great thread idea. I hope it becomes a regular thing.
Honestly, a notebook by the bed has done more for me than any app.
I can relate to this more than I would like to admit.
Saving this thread for later, lots of good suggestions here.
My answer changes every month, but right now it is definitely a long walk after lunch.
This is the kind of thread that makes a forum feel friendly.
Ha, I had exactly the same experience.
Counting this as my small win for the day: I read the whole thread instead of scrolling the news.
I started doing this after reading a similar thread, and it helped a lot.
That sounds lovely. Enjoy it!
Not quite the same, but I found that keeping it simple is what makes it last.
Adding one more to the list: going outside before checking any messages.
I would love to hear how this goes in a month.
This is a good reminder to slow down a bit.
We do something similar at home and it works surprisingly well.
Funny, I was thinking about this exact thing yesterday.
Good luck! Post an update when you can.
Mine is nowhere near as tidy, but it works for me.
The replies in this thread are better than most articles on the topic.
I have no useful advice, I just wanted to say I enjoyed reading this.
Agreed. Small, boring habits beat big plans every time.

forums.name: Help
forums.description: Ask how something works, get unstuck and share answers
forums.guidance: Say what you tried, what you expected and what happened instead. When something solves it, say so.

threads.title: How to ask a good question here
threads.body:
A few tips that get you an answer faster:

- Say what you are trying to do, not only what is broken.
- Include the exact error message and the steps that lead to it.
- Mention versions: operating system, browser, the tool you are using.

And when you solve it yourself, post the fix. Someone will search for it next year.

threads.title: Git: undo the last commit but keep my changes?
threads.body:
I committed to the wrong branch. I want to take the commit back but keep the edits in my working tree, so I can commit them on the right branch.

Is `git reset --soft HEAD~1` the right tool here, or will it bite me later?

threads.title: Laptop fan runs constantly after an update
threads.body:
Since the last system update my laptop fan never stops, even when idle. The task manager shows nothing obviously busy.

Any ideas where to look before I reinstall everything?

threads.title: Which backup strategy for a small team?
threads.body:
Five people, a shared drive and a couple of databases. Right now "backup" means someone copies files to a USB drive on Fridays.

What is a sensible, low-maintenance setup? We have a small budget and no full-time administrator.

threads.title: Spreadsheet formula to sum by month
threads.body:
I have a column of dates and a column of amounts, and I want a total per month on another sheet.

I keep getting lost between SUMIFS and pivot tables. Which is the less painful route?

threads.title: Phone storage is full but I cannot find what is using it
threads.body:
The settings say "System" takes almost half the storage. I have deleted photos and apps and it barely moved.

Is there a safe way to clear it without a factory reset?

threads.title: Regex to match a date like 2024-03-15
threads.body:
I need to pull ISO dates out of log lines. My pattern matches, but it also matches things like 9999-99-99.

Should I validate inside the regex, or match loosely and check the date in code?

threads.title: Wi-Fi drops every evening around 8 pm
threads.body:
Every evening the connection drops for a few seconds, several times an hour. During the day it is fine.

Could this be the neighbours' networks? How do I find out which channel to use?

threads.title: Moving from Windows to Linux: where to start?
threads.body:
I mostly browse, write documents and do a bit of Python. I want to try Linux without losing a weekend to drivers.

Which distribution would you suggest for a cautious beginner, and what should I back up first?

threads.title: Python virtual environments are confusing me
threads.body:
venv, virtualenv, conda, pipx, poetry... I just want my project's packages to stop fighting with each other.

What is the simplest setup that will not confuse me again in six months?

threads.title: Email from my domain lands in spam
threads.body:
We send invoices from our own domain and many of them land in customers' spam folders.

I have heard of SPF, DKIM and DMARC but do not know which one I am missing. How do I check?

threads.title: How do I make a website load faster?
threads.body:
Small business site, mostly images and text. It takes four seconds to load on a phone.

Where should I start: hosting, images, something else?

threads.title: Keyboard shortcuts worth learning?
threads.body:
I still reach for the mouse for almost everything. Which shortcuts saved you the most time once you learned them?

Any operating system is fine.

threads.title: Printer says offline but it is connected
threads.body:
The printer is on the network and I can open its web page, but the computer insists it is offline.

Removing and re-adding it works for a day. Is there a permanent fix?

threads.title: How do I read a stack trace?
threads.body:
I am new to programming, and when something crashes I get a wall of text.

Which line should I look at first, and how do I tell my code apart from the library's?

threads.title: Best way to share large files with a client
threads.body:
I need to send a few gigabytes of video to a client every week. Email obviously fails.

What do you use that is simple for the receiving side?

threads.title: SQL: find rows that have no match in another table
threads.body:
I have `customers` and `orders` and want the customers who never ordered.

I have seen LEFT JOIN with IS NULL, and NOT EXISTS. Is one of them better?

threads.title: Password manager for a family?
threads.body:
I want my parents to stop using the same password everywhere. They are not technical.

Which kind of password manager is easy enough for them and lets us share a few logins?

threads.title: Docker container exits immediately
threads.body:
My container starts and stops right away with exit code 0. The same command works fine on my machine outside Docker.

What am I missing?

threads.title: Time zones in a meeting scheduler
threads.body:
I am building a small scheduling tool. Should I store times in UTC and convert them for display, or store the user's local time?

Daylight saving time is already giving me headaches.

replies: Did you check the logs first? They usually point straight at the problem.
I had the same issue. For me it was a setting that the update had quietly reset.
Can you post the exact error message? It makes guessing much easier.
Try it with a fresh profile or a new user account. If it works there, the problem is in your settings.
Restarting fixed it for me, which is unsatisfying but true.
This is a great question, I have wondered the same thing.
The official documentation covers this, but it is buried. Look for the troubleshooting page.
Make a backup before you try anything drastic.
I would start with the simplest explanation: is everything up to date?
What version are you on? The behaviour changed a couple of releases ago.
Narrow it down first: does it happen every time, or only sometimes?
Thanks, this solved it for me too.
There are several ways to do this, but the boring one is usually the most reliable.
I would avoid that approach. It works until it suddenly does not.
Write down the steps that reproduce it. Half the time that alone shows you the cause.
Not an answer, but I have the same problem and I am following the thread.
Have you tried turning off extensions or plugins one by one?
That is expected behaviour, as odd as it seems. The workaround is to change the default.
Search the project's issue tracker for the error text. Someone has probably reported it.
If it is urgent, roll back to the previous version and investigate later.
When I had this, the key step was clearing the cache. Everything else was a red herring.
Good explanation, thanks for taking the time.
You might be hitting two problems at once. Fix the first error and see what remains.
Try the same thing on another device to rule out the network.
Post an update when you find the cause, I am curious.

forums.name: Showcase
forums.description: Projects, write-ups and things you made
forums.guidance: Share what you built and how. Screenshots, source links and lessons learned are welcome.

threads.title: I built a tiny habit tracker that runs in the terminal
threads.body:
It is a single program that keeps everything in a text file. You mark a habit as done with one command, and it prints a little calendar of the last month.

It started as a weekend project and somehow I have used it every day for three months. Feedback welcome.

threads.title: My first mechanical keyboard build
threads.body:
I soldered every switch myself, broke two of them and learned a lot about patience.

It is a 60% layout with a few custom layers. Typing on it feels great, though my colleagues may disagree about the noise.

threads.title: We open-sourced our internal status page
threads.body:
We used a paid service for years, then wrote a small replacement that reads from our existing health checks.

It is now open source. It does one thing: it shows which services are up, with a short history.

threads.title: Photo series: one street, every hour for a day
threads.body:
I stood on the same corner from 6 am to midnight and took one photo every hour.

The changes in the light are what surprised me most. The 4 pm shot is my favourite.

threads.title: A browser extension that hides comment sections
threads.body:
Some days I just want to read the article. This extension hides comment sections on the sites you choose, with one click to bring them back.

It is about 200 lines and has no tracking at all.

threads.title: Weekend project: a weather station on the balcony
threads.body:
A small board, a temperature and humidity sensor, and a solar panel the size of a postcard.

It posts a reading every five minutes to a page on my home server. Next step: a rain gauge.

threads.title: I rewrote my blog with no JavaScript
threads.body:
My old blog shipped two megabytes of scripts to show text. The new one is plain HTML and CSS generated from Markdown.

Pages load instantly, and I no longer dread updating dependencies.

threads.title: Made a board game for my kids
threads.body:
Cardboard, markers and a lot of rule changes after play-testing with two very honest critics.

It is a cooperative game about getting a cat home before it rains. Happy to share the rules if anyone wants them.

threads.title: A command-line tool to rename photos by the date taken
threads.body:
My photo folders were full of IMG_4821.jpg. This tool reads the date from each photo and renames it to something sortable.

It has a dry-run mode, because I learned that lesson the hard way.

threads.title: Restored a radio from the 1980s
threads.body:
I found it at a flea market, completely silent. After replacing a few capacitors and cleaning every contact, it plays again.

The smell of the warm electronics is half the charm.

threads.title: A plain-text accounting setup that works for me
threads.body:
Every transaction is a line in a text file, and a small script turns the file into monthly reports.

It took a while to set up, but now I can answer "where did the money go?" in seconds.

threads.title: Launched my first mobile app
threads.body:
It is a simple app for splitting bills between friends. No accounts, no ads, everything stays on the phone.

It has 40 users, most of whom I know personally. Still counts!

threads.title: Built a bookshelf from reclaimed wood
threads.body:
The wood came from an old fence. Lots of sanding, a few splinters and one shelf that is ever so slightly crooked.

I am calling the crooked one a design feature.

threads.title: Visualising a year of my running data
threads.body:
I exported a year of runs and made a few charts: distance by week, pace against temperature and favourite routes on a map.

It turns out I run slower in summer, which I could have guessed.

threads.title: A small library for reading configuration files
threads.body:
It reads TOML, reports errors with line numbers and refuses unknown keys, so typos do not pass silently.

It is small on purpose. Contributions and bug reports are welcome.

threads.title: Knitted my first sweater
threads.body:
Six months, three restarts and one sleeve that is longer than the other.

I am wearing it anyway.

threads.title: A self-hosted photo gallery for the family
threads.body:
The grandparents wanted to see photos without joining a social network. Now there is a private gallery on a tiny server at home.

Uploading is drag and drop, viewing is a link. That is all they needed.

threads.title: Pixel art for a game jam
threads.body:
Our team made a small puzzle game in 48 hours. I did the art, all of it 16 by 16 pixels.

We did not win, but people played it to the end, which felt like winning.

threads.title: Turned an old phone into a kitchen dashboard
threads.body:
An old phone on the kitchen wall now shows the weather, the bus times and the shopping list.

It cost nothing and the whole family actually uses it.

threads.title: Write-up: what I learned building a search feature
threads.body:
Search seemed easy until people typed things I never expected: typos, plurals, emoji.

I wrote down the lessons, from splitting text into words to ranking results so that they feel right.

replies: This is really neat. How long did it take you?
Love it. Is the source available anywhere?
The attention to detail shows. Great work.
I have been meaning to build something like this for ages. You just saved me the trouble.
Bookmarked. I will try it this weekend.
What was the hardest part?
It is great to see something small and focused that does one thing well.
Congratulations on shipping it, that is the hardest step.
I would happily pay for this, by the way.
The write-up is as good as the project. Thanks for sharing the mistakes too.
This inspired me to finally finish my own side project.
Any plans for what comes next?
Simple and useful. Exactly the kind of thing I like to see here.
How did you decide what to leave out? That is always the hard part for me.
Did you run into any surprises along the way?
I tried something similar and gave up halfway. Respect for finishing.
The photos are lovely.
I shared this with a friend who will love it.
Clean, small and well explained. Nice.
What tools did you use?
This is the best kind of weekend project.
Would you do anything differently if you started again?
Following this one. Looking forward to updates.
Really impressive for a first attempt.
Thanks for posting this, it made my day.

forums.name: Technology
forums.description: Software, hardware, the web and the tools we use
forums.guidance: News, opinions and comparisons. Link to your sources and keep it civil.

threads.title: What is in your everyday toolkit?
threads.body:
Editor, terminal, browser, note-taking app: what do you use every day, and what did you drop recently?

I finally replaced three note apps with a folder of Markdown files.

threads.title: Are static sites making a comeback?
threads.body:
More and more projects I follow are moving their sites to plain generated HTML.

Is this a real trend or just my corner of the internet? What do you use for small sites?

threads.title: Laptop recommendations for development
threads.body:
My laptop is six years old and compiling anything takes a coffee break.

What would you buy today for general development, mostly backend work and a few containers?

threads.title: Dark mode: do you actually use it?
threads.body:
Every app has it now. I switch to dark in the evening and back to light during the day.

Do you stick to one, let it follow the system, or never touch it?

threads.title: How do you keep up with security updates?
threads.body:
Between the operating system, the browser, the phone and a handful of servers, something always needs an update.

Do you automate it, schedule it, or just react to warnings?

threads.title: Self-hosting: is it worth it?
threads.body:
I run a few services at home: files, photos, a password manager. It is fun, but it is also another job.

Where do you draw the line between hosting things yourself and paying someone else?

threads.title: SQLite in production: who is doing it?
threads.body:
For small and medium sites, a single SQLite file seems to work far better than its reputation suggests.

Is anyone running it in production? What surprised you?

threads.title: Favourite command-line tools
threads.body:
Beyond the classics, which small tools have earned a permanent place in your shell?

Mine: a fuzzy finder and a faster grep. I would not go back.

threads.title: Is email still the best notification channel?
threads.body:
Every service wants to push notifications to my phone, but email is still the only place I reliably look.

How do you handle notifications without drowning in them?

threads.title: Thoughts on AI coding assistants
threads.body:
I use one for boilerplate and tests, but I still review every line.

Where do you find them genuinely helpful, and where do they get in the way?

threads.title: Mechanical keyboards: hype or worth it?
threads.body:
I am thinking of getting one. Is typing really better, or is it mostly a hobby?

Recommendations for quiet switches are welcome, for the sake of my household.

threads.title: How much memory is enough these days?
threads.body:
Browsers, editors and a few containers eat memory faster than I can buy it.

How much do you have, and do you ever hit the limit?

threads.title: The case for boring technology
threads.body:
Every time I chose the exciting new database, I spent the next year learning its corner cases.

Now I pick the boring, well-understood option unless there is a strong reason not to. Agree?

threads.title: Do you still use RSS?
threads.body:
I follow about 80 sites with a feed reader. It is calm, ad-free and in chronological order.

Anyone else? Which reader do you use?

threads.title: One big screen or two smaller ones?
threads.body:
I am replacing my two monitors and cannot decide between one ultrawide and two normal screens.

What do you prefer for programming, and why?

threads.title: Accessibility basics every website should get right
threads.body:
Alt text, real buttons, visible focus, enough contrast, and everything working without a mouse.

What else would you add to the list of basics that are too often missed?

threads.title: Backups: what is your setup?
threads.body:
I follow the 3-2-1 rule, more or less: two copies at home and one somewhere else.

What do you back up, how often, and when did you last test a restore?

threads.title: Why are apps getting so large?
threads.body:
A note-taking app on my phone is 300 MB. My first computer's hard drive was smaller.

Is this just the cost of modern frameworks, or are we getting lazy?

threads.title: Open-source maintainers: how do you avoid burnout?
threads.body:
I maintain a small library with a few thousand users. Issues arrive faster than I can answer them.

How do other maintainers set boundaries without abandoning the project?

threads.title: Privacy-friendly analytics for a small site
threads.body:
I want to know which pages people read without tracking individuals or showing a cookie banner.

What do you use, and is reading the server logs good enough?

replies: Strong agree. Boring and reliable wins in the long run.
I switched last year and have not looked back.
It depends a lot on the use case, but for most small projects the simple option is fine.
Interesting take. I see it differently, but I appreciate the reasoning.
The real cost is the maintenance, not the initial setup.
I tested both for a month and ended up somewhere in the middle.
Good question. I would love to see some actual numbers on this.
Whatever you choose, make sure you can get your data out later.
Hardware has never been cheaper, but my patience for slow software has never been lower.
This matches my experience exactly.
I used to think so too, until it failed at the worst possible moment.
Automate it if you can. Anything that relies on remembering will eventually be forgotten.
Great list. I would add one thing: read the changelog before upgrading.
Plain text has outlived every app I have ever used.
The best tool is the one you already know well.
I am still on a setup from ten years ago and it does everything I need.
Worth it for me, but I enjoy tinkering. If you do not, pay someone else.
Measure before you optimise. Half my guesses about slowness were wrong.
There is a good conference talk on exactly this topic, worth looking up.
I tried this at work, and the hardest part was convincing people, not the technology.
Fair point, but you are underestimating how much the defaults matter.
Count me in the "still uses it every day" camp.
Security updates are the one thing I always automate.
This thread is a goldmine, thanks everyone.
Every few years the industry rediscovers this idea, and it is right every time.

forums.name: Feedback
forums.description: Suggestions and questions about this forum
forums.guidance: One idea or question per thread. Say what you would like to change and why.

threads.title: Suggestion: a weekly digest email
threads.body:
I do not visit every day, but I would love a short email on Sunday with the most active threads of the week.

Would anyone else use this?

threads.title: The dark theme is easy on the eyes
threads.body:
I just switched to the dark theme and wanted to say it is really comfortable for late-night reading.

Thanks to whoever worked on it.

threads.title: Could we have a board for job postings?
threads.body:
Every now and then someone asks about jobs in General. A board of its own with a simple template might keep things tidy.

Thoughts?

threads.title: Notifications: too many or just right?
threads.body:
I get a notification for every reply in threads I have posted in. Useful, but it adds up.

Do people prefer control per thread, or a daily summary?

threads.title: Would a chat room be useful?
threads.body:
Some questions need a quick back-and-forth rather than a thread. Would a chat room next to the forum help, or would it split the community?

I can see it going either way.

threads.title: Suggestion: a short pinned guide in each board
threads.body:
New members often ask the same questions. A short pinned thread in each board explaining what belongs there would help.

Happy to help write them.

threads.title: Idea: mark the reply that solved a question
threads.body:
In Help it would be useful if the person who asked could mark the reply that solved their problem.

Future visitors would find the answer without reading the whole thread.

threads.title: What are the rules on self-promotion?
threads.body:
I would like to share a project that I sell. Is that fine in Showcase, or is there a better place?

I do not want to come across as spam.

threads.title: Ideas for a community event?
threads.body:
It might be fun to organise something together: an online meetup, a reading club, a small coding challenge.

What would you join?

threads.title: Request: tags as well as boards
threads.body:
Some threads fit two boards. Tags would let us find, say, every thread about backups, wherever it was posted.

Would that be too much complexity?

threads.title: Is there an API?
threads.body:
I would like to write a small script that shows new threads on my desktop. Is there an API, and does it need a token?

Just looking for a pointer to the documentation.

threads.title: Idea: a monthly "what I made" thread
threads.body:
Showcase is great, but a monthly round-up thread might encourage people with smaller projects to post too.

Anyone up for it?

threads.title: Collect the best threads in one place?
threads.body:
Some of the best threads get buried after a few weeks. A list of highlights would help newcomers find them.

They deserve a second life.

threads.title: How are moderators chosen?
threads.body:
Curious how moderation works here. Are moderators volunteers, and can members offer to help?

Not complaining at all, the forum is very well run.

threads.title: Which image formats can I upload?
threads.body:
I want to add screenshots to a thread. Which formats and sizes are allowed, and are images resized automatically?

A short note on the posting page would help.

threads.title: Please keep the forum fast
threads.body:
One of the reasons I like it here is that pages load instantly, even on a bad connection.

Whatever new features come, please keep that.

threads.title: Etiquette: replying to old threads
threads.body:
Is it fine to reply to a thread from a year ago if I have something useful to add, or should I start a new one?

Different forums have different rules on this.

threads.title: Can I download my data or delete my account?
threads.body:
Not planning to leave, but I like to know before I settle in anywhere: can I download my data and delete my account later?

Where would I find that?

threads.title: Suggestion: a glossary for newcomers
threads.body:
Some threads are full of abbreviations that newcomers will not know. A short glossary, kept up by the community, could help.

I can start one if people are interested.

threads.title: Thank you, everyone
threads.body:
This is one of the few places online where people answer questions patiently and disagree politely.

Just wanted to say thanks to the members and the moderators.

replies: +1, I would use this every week.
Good idea, though I worry it would add noise.
I like things the way they are, but I would not mind trying this.
Thanks for raising it. Small things like this add up.
